note: One of the legal ways of hunting: salto, espera, batida, montaria, corricão, aproximação, cetraria, com furão (each its own entry). 'processo' alone in this sense → 'method'; 'processos de caça' → 'hunting methods'; 'pelo processo de X' → 'by the X method', X as its entry gives it.

Method in which the hunter walks the ground, alone or in a line, with or without dogs, and shoots the game it flushes. 'de salto' → 'walked-up'; 'caça de salto' → 'walked-up hunting'; 'caçar de salto' → 'hunt walked-up'; 'pelo processo de salto' → 'by the walked-up method'; a bare option ('De salto', 'Salto') → 'Walked-up'. Never 'jump', 'jump hunting', 'walk-up' or 'rough shooting'.

Method in which the hunter waits at a fixed post (a hide, a high seat, a stand by water) for the game to come to him. 'à espera', 'de espera' → 'from a hide'; 'caça à espera' → 'hunting from a hide'; 'pelo processo de espera' → 'by the hide method'; 'locais de espera' → 'hide positions'; 'as esperas', 'nas esperas' → 'the hides', 'in the hides'; a bare option ('À espera', 'De espera') → 'From a hide'. Never 'waiting' or 'ambush'.

Method in which the hunters stand at fixed posts while beaters (batedores), with or without dogs, drive the game towards them. 'de batida' → 'driven'; 'caça de batida' → 'driven hunting'; 'pelo processo de batida' → 'by the driven method'; 'caçar de batida' → 'hunt in a driven hunt'; 'batidas às raposas' → 'driven hunts for foxes'; a bare option ('Batida', 'De batida') → 'Driven hunt', 'Driven'. Not montaria, which is a big-game drive with packs of hounds.

Portuguese big-game hunt, chiefly wild boar and deer, in which packs of hounds worked by houndsmen (matilheiros) drive the game towards hunters at fixed posts. No English equivalent, so it stays in Portuguese (D4): give the gloss in parentheses at its first use in a sentence, plain 'montaria' after. 'montarias' → 'montarias'; 'montarias aos javalis' → 'montarias for wild boar'; 'de montaria' → 'by montaria'.

Method in which game (hare, fox) is chased down by dogs, the hunter on foot or on horseback, with or without a stick (pau) and never with a firearm. 'a corricão' → 'by coursing'; 'caça à lebre a corricão' → 'hare coursing'; 'caça à raposa a corricão' → 'fox coursing'; 'processo de caça a corricão' → 'coursing'; a bare option ('Corricão', 'A corricão') → 'Coursing'.

Big-game method in which the hunter moves towards a particular animal (exemplar) to shoot it. 'de aproximação', 'caça de aproximação' → 'stalking'; 'processo de aproximação' → 'stalking method'; 'pelo processo de aproximação' → 'by stalking'; a bare option ('De aproximação') → 'Stalking'.

Method in which game is taken by a trained bird of prey (ave de presa); the hunter may use hunting dogs and a stick, never a firearm. 'de cetraria', 'caça de cetraria' → 'falconry'; 'pelo processo de cetraria' → 'by falconry'; a bare option ('Cetraria', 'De cetraria') → 'Falconry'. The person is a cetreiro (falconer).

The domestic ferret, used to bolt rabbits from their burrows, and the hunting method that uses it. 'com furão' in a list of methods → 'with a ferret'; 'furões' → 'ferrets'; 'deter, transportar ou usar furão' → 'keep, transport or use a ferret'.
Assistants (auxiliares) who walk through cover to drive game towards the hunters in a batida or montaria. Singular 'batedor' → 'beater'.
Assistants who search for, pursue and flush big game with a pack of hounds (matilha), as in a montaria. Singular 'matilheiro' → 'houndsman'; 'matilha' → 'pack'.
Assistants who set and work the decoys (negaças); they do not pursue game with dogs. Singular 'negaceiro' → 'decoy handler'.

A person who helps a hunter while hunting without being one of the line of hunters: beaters, houndsmen, decoy handlers. 'auxiliares' → 'assistants'; 'auxiliares do caçador', 'auxiliares de caça' → 'hunter's assistants', 'hunting assistants'. 'auxílio' is a different word → 'help' ('com o auxílio de 10 cães' → 'with the help of 10 dogs').
The hunters walking abreast in walked-up hunting, or standing at their posts in a drive. 'fazer parte da linha de caçadores' → 'be part of the line of hunters'.
A person who hunts by falconry. 'carta de caçador de cetreiro', 'carta de cetreiro' → 'falconer's hunter's certificate', 'falconer's certificate'.
A hunter who uses a crossbow (besta). Paired in the bank with 'arqueiro' → 'archer': 'O Arqueiro ou Besteiro' → 'The archer or crossbowman'.
The body or person granted a hunting zone (zona de caça) by the state and running it under its management plan.

Whoever holds the legal right over the land: owner, tenant or manager. 'sem consentimento de quem de direito' → 'without the consent of the person entitled'; 'com autorização de quem de direito' → 'with the authorisation of the person entitled'.

The permanent qualification issued after passing this exam, renewed at intervals, that a person must hold to hunt; the subject of this app. Not the licença de caça, the hunting licence bought for a period. 'titular da carta de caçador' → 'holder of the hunter's certificate'.

The permit, bought for a period and a region or the whole country, needed on top of the hunter's certificate to hunt. Kinds: licença regional de caça, licença nacional de caça, licença de aves aquáticas (each its own entry). 'licenças de caça' → 'hunting licences'. British spelling 'licence' for the noun.
A hunting licence valid in one hunting region (região cinegética).
A hunting licence valid throughout the country, in every hunting region.
The extra licence needed to hunt waterfowl (aves aquáticas), on top of a regional or national hunting licence. The bank also writes 'licença para caçar aves aquáticas' → 'licence to hunt waterfowl'.
The licence a hunting dog must have once it is older than the age the law sets.
One of the regions the mainland is divided into for hunting licences and rules. 'numa única região cinegética' → 'in a single hunting region'.

The span of time in which a given species may be hunted, set in the hunting calendar. 'o período venatório de uma espécie' → 'the open season for a species'; 'limite máximo do período venatório' → 'maximum limit of the open season'; 'fora do período venatório da espécie' → 'outside the species' open season'. Not época venatória (the hunting year).
The annual period from 1 June to 31 May of the following year to which the hunting rules and calendar apply. Not período venatório (the open season of one species). Never 'hunting season'.
The ministerial order (portaria) published each year that lists the species that may be hunted, their open seasons, methods and bag limits. 'calendário venatório anual' → 'annual hunting calendar'.

Legal phrase for the activity of hunting. 'É proibido o exercício da caça' → 'The practice of hunting is prohibited'; 'no exercício da caça', 'durante o exercício da caça' → 'in the practice of hunting', 'during the practice of hunting'; 'fora do exercício da caça' → 'outside the practice of hunting'. 'exercício venatório' means the same → 'practice of hunting'.

Legal phrase for hunting itself. 'exercer o ato venatório', 'praticar o ato venatório' → 'carry out the act of hunting'. 'venatório', 'venatória' as an adjective → 'hunting' ('atividades de carácter venatório' → 'activities of a hunting nature').

A notice issued and posted by the authority (here the ICNF) setting local conditions, such as where and when a method may be used. 'definidos em edital do ICNF' → 'set in a public notice of the ICNF'; 'nos locais e condições definidos em edital' → 'in the places and on the conditions set in a public notice'; 'por edital' → 'by public notice'.

A regulation issued by a minister; the hunting calendar and the lists of game species are set by portaria. 'em portaria' → 'by ministerial order'; 'portaria do calendário venatório' → 'ministerial order of the hunting calendar'. When cited by number (Portaria 67/2024) the name is copied unchanged.
Acronym of the Instituto da Conservação da Natureza e das Florestas, the state body for nature, forests and hunting that issues licences and public notices. Copied unchanged (D4, proper name).

pt: Instituto de Conservação da Natureza e das Florestas
en: Instituto de Conservação da Natureza e das Florestas
note: Proper name of the ICNF (in English, the Institute for Nature Conservation and Forests), copied unchanged as the question writes it (D4); the bank spells it both 'Instituto de Conservação…' and 'Instituto da Conservação…'.

pt: plano de ordenamento e exploração cinegética
note: The approved plan under which a hunting zone is run, setting what may be hunted, when and how. Acronym 'POEC' copied unchanged. The bank also writes 'planos de ordenamento cinegético ou exploração' → 'game management or exploitation plans'.
A simpler approved plan for a hunting zone, the alternative to the POEC. Acronym 'PG' copied unchanged.

Planned management of game and its habitat. 'ordenamento do coelho-bravo' → 'management of the wild rabbit'; 'ordenamento cinegético' → 'game management'. The participle 'ordenados' → 'managed' (see terrenos cinegéticos ordenados).

A criminal offence under the hunting law (hunting without a certificate, in an area where one has no right of access, non-game species, and so on), as against a contra ordenação. 'constitui crime de caça' → 'constitutes a hunting crime'.
A breach punished by a fine, not a crime. The bank writes it as two words; standard spelling is 'contraordenação'. 'contra ordenação grave' → 'serious administrative offence'.

Of a certificate or licence: ceases to be valid by law. 'A carta de caçador caduca' → 'The hunter's certificate lapses'; 'caducidade' → 'expiry' ('o final da sua caducidade' → 'the end of its expiry'). Of leaves, 'folha caduca' → 'deciduous' ('bosques de folha caduca' → 'deciduous woods').

A single animal or bird of a species. 'determinado exemplar de caça maior' → 'a particular individual of big game'; 'exemplares dos dois sexos' → 'individuals of both sexes'. Never 'specimen' or 'copy'.
The lottery by which places to hunt in a municipal hunting zone are allotted. 'contemplado em sorteio público' → 'drawn in a public draw'.
The public holidays fixed by law for the whole country, as against 'feriados municipais' → 'municipal public holidays'.
Land where hunting is permitted. Singular 'terreno cinegético' → 'hunting ground'. Split into managed (ordenados) and unmanaged (não ordenados), each its own entry.
Land where hunting is prohibited, such as protection areas, game refuges and no-hunting areas. Singular 'terreno não cinegético' → 'non-hunting ground'.
Hunting grounds organised as hunting zones (zonas de caça) and run under an approved plan. The bank also shortens it to 'terrenos ordenados' → 'managed grounds'.

Hunting grounds outside any hunting zone, where the general rules apply (with a firearm, only on Thursdays, Sundays and compulsory national public holidays). The bank also shortens it to 'terrenos não ordenados' → 'unmanaged grounds'.

A managed area granted for hunting under an approved plan; the kinds are national, municipal, tourist and association hunting zones. 'zonas de caça' → 'hunting zones'; 'em zonas de caça' → 'in hunting zones'.
Hunting zones run by the state. Singular 'zona de caça nacional' → 'national hunting zone'.
A hunting zone open to hunters in general, run by a local body, where places are allotted by public draw. Plural 'zonas de caça municipais' → 'municipal hunting zones'.
A commercially run hunting zone open to any hunter who pays and keeps its own rules. Plural 'zonas de caça turísticas' → 'tourist hunting zones'.
Hunting zones run by a hunters' association for its members and their guests. Singular 'zona de caça associativa' → 'association hunting zone'.
Areas where the law bans hunting for protection; one kind of non-hunting ground. Singular 'área de proteção' → 'protection area'. Not 'protected areas' (nature reserves).
An area closed to hunting so that game can breed and shelter; the ban applies only where it is signposted. 'áreas de refúgio de caça' → 'game refuge areas'.

An area licensed for training dogs and birds of prey and for shooting practice on farmed game. 'campos de treino de caça' → 'hunting training grounds'; the bank also shortens it to 'campos de treino' → 'training grounds'.
Land closed to hunting at the request of its owner, who has exercised the right to no hunting (direito à não caça). Singular 'área de não caça' → 'no-hunting area'.
A landowner's legal right to keep hunting off his land. 'áreas de direito à não caça' → 'areas under the right to no hunting'.
A fenced area holding livestock; hunting there is banned where it is signposted. 'aparcamentos de gado' → 'livestock enclosures'.

The strip of land around a place in which hunting is also banned. 'bem como numa faixa de proteção de 500 metros' → 'as well as in a protection strip of 500 metres'. 'faixa envolvente' → 'surrounding strip'.
Towns and villages, inhabited places. 'nos povoados' → 'in settlements'.

Marked with the legal signs. Agrees with its noun: 'devidamente sinalizados', 'devidamente sinalizadas' → 'duly signposted'. 'sinalização' → 'signposting'; 'sinalizados com o sinal de proibição de caçar' → 'signposted with the no-hunting sign'.
The official sign that closes land to hunting (the picture in questions 373, 375, 394 and 397). 'Proibição de caçar' as an option → 'No hunting'.
'áreas de jurisdição marítima' → 'areas under maritime jurisdiction': coastal and tidal areas under the maritime authority, which count as hunting grounds.
Rivers, lakes and reservoirs, as against maritime areas.
Lakes, ponds, reservoirs and the like. 'até 200 m dos planos de água' → 'up to 200 m from bodies of water'.
'zonas húmidas' → 'wetlands'. Not 'humid zone'.

Means both the activity (hunting) and the animals hunted (game). Activity: 'a caça à perdiz', 'na caça aos patos' → 'partridge hunting', 'in duck hunting'; 'caça de salto' and the other methods as their entries give them. Animals: 'a caça' in biology and raptor questions → 'game'; 'espécies de caça' → 'game species'; 'caça maior', 'caça menor' → 'big game', 'small game'. 'caçar à', 'caçar aos' + species → 'hunt' + species ('caçar só às narcejas' → 'hunt only snipe').
Wild boar, deer, mouflon and the like. 'espécies de caça maior' → 'big-game species'; 'na caça maior' → 'in big-game hunting'.

Rabbit, hare, fox, partridge, quail, pigeons, ducks and the like. 'espécies de caça menor' → 'small-game species'; 'caça menor sedentária' → 'resident small game'; 'caça menor aquáticas' → 'aquatic small game'.

Species that the law allows to be hunted. Singular 'espécie cinegética' → 'game species'. The adjective 'cinegético' → 'game' for animals and populations ('populações cinegéticas' → 'game populations') and 'hunting' for land and administration ('terrenos cinegéticos' → 'hunting grounds', 'região cinegética' → 'hunting region', 'atividades de caráter cinegético' → 'hunting activities').
Species that may not be hunted. Singular 'espécie não cinegética' → 'non-game species'; 'não é cinegética' → 'is not a game species'.

Game mammals. 'de pelo' as an option → 'Furred game'; 'de pelo e de pena' → 'furred and feathered game'. The bank also spells it 'pêlo'. Of a dog's coat, 'pelo' → 'coat' ('de pelo liso' → 'smooth-coated').
Game birds. 'de pena' as an option → 'Feathered game'.
Ducks and the other water birds that need the waterfowl licence. 'caçar aves aquáticas' → 'hunt waterfowl'.
Of a species: present all year, not migrating. 'sedentário', 'sedentárias', 'sedentários' → 'resident'; 'caça menor sedentária' → 'resident small game'.

A migrant that spends the winter in Portugal and breeds elsewhere. 'invernante' alone → 'wintering'; 'invernam em Portugal' → 'winter in Portugal'. 'migradora', 'migrador' alone → 'migratory'; 'parcialmente migrador' → 'partially migratory'.
A migrant that comes to Portugal to breed in spring and summer. 'estival' alone → 'summer'; 'migradoras estivais' → 'summer visitors'.
A migrant seen only on passage, in spring or autumn, between its breeding and wintering grounds.

To kill game by hunting. 'abateu 10 codornizes' → 'killed 10 quail'; 'pode abater por dia de caça' → 'may kill per hunting day'; 'o abate' → 'the killing' ('o abate de menos de 50% dos efetivos' → 'the killing of less than 50% of the stock').
The number of animals in a game population. 'abater 60% dos efetivos' → 'kill 60% of the stock'.
Releasing animals to rebuild a wild population. 'realizar repovoamentos' → 'carry out restocking'; 'nos repovoamentos' → 'in restocking'.
Releases of farmed game, for example for shooting on a hunting training ground.

To make game break cover. 'levantar espécies de caça maior' → 'flush big-game species'; 'espécies levantadas por batedores' → 'species flushed by beaters'. Not 'levantar voo' → 'take off', said of birds.

Devices worked by the hunter to imitate the voice of game and draw it in (duck, fox, deer calls). Singular 'chamariz' → 'lure call'. Battery-powered devices to attract game are banned. Not negaças (decoys).
Figures of birds, real or artificial, set out to draw birds within range. 'uso de negaças' → 'use of decoys'. Not chamarizes (lure calls).
The stick a hunter may carry in coursing, walked-up hunting and falconry. 'com ou sem pau' → 'with or without a stick'; 'Pau e cavalo' → 'Stick and horse'.
Lead shot over 4,5 mm in diameter; banned for hunting. 'cartuchos carregados com zagalotes' → 'cartridges loaded with buckshot'.
Small pellets in a shotgun cartridge. 'cartuchos carregados com chumbos' → 'cartridges loaded with shot'; 'chumbos de diâmetro superior a 4,5 mm' → 'shot of diameter greater than 4,5 mm'.
A single projectile in a shotgun cartridge, used for big game. 'cartuchos carregados com bala' → 'cartridges loaded with a slug'.
Shotgun ammunition. British 'cartridges', never 'shells'. 'cartuchos vazios' → 'spent cartridges'.
Smooth-bore hunting guns. Singular 'espingarda caçadeira' → 'shotgun'.
'armas de fogo' → 'firearms'; 'sem arma de fogo' → 'without a firearm'. 'armas de caça' → 'hunting guns'; 'armas semiautomáticas' → 'semi-automatic guns'.
'arco ou besta' → 'bow or crossbow'. In this bank it never means 'beast'.
The arrows shot from a crossbow. 'flechas ou virotões' → 'arrows or bolts'; singular 'virotão' → 'bolt'.
The case in which arrows or bolts are carried.
The catch that stops a crossbow from being fired by accident.
The cutting blades of a broadhead arrow or bolt tip, required for big game. 'Com lâminas' → 'With blades'; 'duas lâminas com barbela' → 'two blades with a barb'.
A backward-pointing hook on an arrow or bolt tip. 'Com barbela' → 'With a barb'. Not farpas (prongs).
Sharp points on an arrow tip. 'Duas farpas' → 'Two prongs'. Not barbela (barb).
Of an arrow or bolt tip: bullet-shaped, without blades (a field point); not permitted for big game.
A raised platform from which the hunter waits for and shoots game. 'a partir de uma plataforma elevada' → 'from a high seat'.
In hare coursing, the dog that finds and starts the hare before the greyhounds run it. 'cães de busca' → 'search dogs'.
Sighthounds that run game down by speed, used in coursing. 'cão galgo', 'cães galgos' → 'greyhound', 'greyhounds'.
Dogs that freeze to show where game is hiding. The verb 'parar' in this sense → 'point' ('além de "parar"' → 'as well as "pointing"').
From 'cobrar': of a dog, to bring back shot game. 'cobra bem na água e em terra' → 'retrieves well in water and on land'; 'cães que cobram bem' → 'dogs that retrieve well'. Never 'snake'.
Hounds that hunt as a pack (equipagem), as in a montaria.
The trail left by wounded game. 'cães de pista de sangue de caça maior' → 'big-game blood-trail dogs'; 'seguir pistas de sangue de caça maior' → 'follow blood trails of big game'.
Popular name for the medium podengo, the rabbit-hunting dog; the questions ask about the name itself, so it stays in Portuguese with its gloss (D4). 'cão coelheiro' → 'coelheiro (rabbit dog)'.

Portuguese hound breed (in English, the Portuguese Podengo), used for furred game. 'podengo pequeno', 'podengo médio', 'podengo grande' → 'small podengo', 'medium podengo', 'large podengo'; 'podengos' → 'podengos'.
Portuguese pointing breed, used for feathered game. 'perdigueiro português' → 'Portuguese pointer'. Not the English breed 'pointer', which the bank names 'pointer'.
German pointing breed, smooth or wire-coated ('de pelo liso ou cerdoso' → 'smooth- or wire-coated').
Short-legged scent hounds used to follow the blood trail of wounded big game; no single English breed name, so it stays in Portuguese with its gloss (D4). Singular 'baixote'.

The French pointing breed known in Britain as the Brittany. Other breed names in the bank are English already: 'setter irlandês' → 'Irish setter', 'setter inglês' → 'English setter', 'pointer', 'beagle', 'fox-terrier' → 'fox terrier'.
English pack hound. 'Os Fox-hound' → 'Foxhounds'. Question 494 misspells it 'Fox-houd'; render that as 'foxhound' too.

The bright, often metallic patch on the wing of many ducks. 'espelho' alone in the same sense → 'speculum' ('espelho azul' → 'blue speculum'; 'espelho com reflexos metálicos' → 'speculum with a metallic sheen'). Never 'wing mirror'.
A pale band along the wing of diving ducks. 'franja alar branca ou pálida' → 'white or pale wing bar'.
A visible difference between male and female of the same species. 'dimorfismo sexual acentuado' → 'marked sexual dimorphism'.
Ducks that feed at the surface by up-ending, such as the mallard and gadwall. Singular 'pato de superfície' → 'dabbling duck'. Never 'surface ducks'.
Ducks that feed by diving, such as the common pochard. Singular 'pato mergulhador' → 'diving duck'.
Ducks of the open sea and coast.

The mating season of mammals. Of deer, boar and mouflon → 'rut' ('o cio do corço' → 'the roe deer rut'; 'época do cio' → 'rutting season'). Of the fox, and 'o cio das fêmeas' → 'heat' ('durante o cio das fêmeas' → 'while the females are in heat').
The bellowing call of the red deer stag in the rut. Question 150 asks what the word names, so render it 'roar' and let the options define it.
The pair of antlers of a deer, as a whole. 'armações' → 'antlers' ('perdem as armações' → 'cast their antlers'). 'A cabeça do gamo', meaning the fallow buck's antlers → 'the fallow buck's head'.
The two main branches that make up a deer's antlers. 'duas hastes espalmadas' → 'two palmate beams'; 'hastes cilíndricas' → 'cylindrical beams'; 'hastes ramificadas' → 'branched beams'.
The furred skin that covers a deer's antlers while they grow.
The pale patch round the tail of the roe deer, shaped differently in buck and doe.
The wild boar's lower canines, its main weapons. Paired with amoladeiras (whetters), the upper canines that sharpen them.
The wild boar's upper canines, against which the lower tusks (navalhas) are sharpened.

The animal hunted by a predator or a hunter. 'ave de presa' → 'bird of prey'; 'populações presa' → 'prey populations'. Of the wild boar, 'presas' → 'tusks' ('presas mais desenvolvidas nos machos' → 'larger tusks in the males').
Groups of wild boar. Singular 'vara' → 'sounder'. In 'Varas ou companhias' → 'Sounders or companhias'.
Another name for groups of wild boar, beside varas; no separate English word, so it stays in Portuguese with its gloss (D4). Singular 'companhia'.
A wild boar piglet under six months old, named after its striped coat (pelagem raiada → 'striped coat'). No English equivalent; stays in Portuguese with its gloss (D4). Plural 'listados'.
A young wild boar between six months and one year old. No English equivalent; stays in Portuguese with its gloss (D4).
A young pig; a wrong option beside listado and farropo in question 132, so it keeps the Portuguese with its gloss (D4).
A young pig, here offered as a name for the boar's young.
Young rabbits. Singular 'láparo' → 'rabbit kit'. Not lebrachos (leverets).
Young hares. Singular 'lebracho' → 'leveret'.
Young partridges. Singular 'perdigoto' → 'partridge chick'.
The young of an animal. 'crias ou ovos' → 'young or eggs'; 'a cria de javali' → 'the young of the wild boar'. The verb 'criar' → 'breed' ('época de criação' → 'breeding season').
The young born together to a mammal. 'ninhadas por ano' → 'litters a year'.
The female red deer. 'cervas' → 'hinds'. The male is a stag ('veado macho' → 'red deer stag').
The female fallow deer. 'gamelas' → 'fallow does'; 'gama' is a synonym ('Gama ou gamela' → 'Fallow doe (gama or gamela)').
The female roe deer.

en: terçó (tiercel, the male bird of prey)
note: In falconry, the male of a bird of prey, smaller than the female. Stays in Portuguese with its gloss (D4), since question 503 names it.
Mounds of stones, branches and earth built to give rabbits burrows where the ground is hard to dig. No English equivalent; stays in Portuguese with its gloss (D4).
The ten long feathers at the tip of the wing. 'rémiges' alone → 'flight feathers'.
The bare lower legs of a bird. Singular 'tarso' → 'tarsus'.
The horny spikes on the back of a partridge's legs.
The replacing of a bird's feathers. 'a muda das penas' → 'the moult of the feathers'. British spelling 'moult'.
The lower back of a bird, above the tail. 'uropígio branco' → 'white rump'.
The bare plate above the bill of the moorhen and the coot.
A mammal's fur. 'pelagem raiada' → 'striped coat'.
A bird of the order of fowl, partridges and quail. 'o mais pequeno galináceo europeu' → 'the smallest European galliform'.
The deer family. 'os cervídeos portugueses' → 'the Portuguese deer'.
Farmland left unsown for a season. 'pousios e terras cultivadas' → 'fallow land and cultivated land'. Not fallow deer (gamo).
Open grazed woodland of holm oak, typical of the south.
Low dense shrubs. 'zonas de mato abundante' → 'areas of abundant scrub'; 'matos' → 'scrub'. Not matagais (thickets).
Dense tall scrub. Singular 'matagal' → 'thicket'.
Fields of growing cereal. 'zonas cerealíferas', 'culturas cerealíferas' → 'cereal-growing areas', 'cereal crops'.
Vegetation in which game hides. 'grande densidade de coberto' → 'dense cover'. As a participle, 'coberto de' → 'covered with' ('coberto de plantas secas' → 'covered with dry plants').
The stalks left after harvest. 'queima de restolhos' → 'stubble burning'.
In falconry, the trained bird. 'aves de presa' → 'birds of prey'. Same meaning as aves de rapina.
Hawks, eagles, falcons, kites, owls and vultures, all fully protected. 'rapinas diurnas' → 'diurnal birds of prey'; 'ave de rapina' → 'bird of prey'. Same meaning as ave de presa.

Falconry with short-winged hawks such as the goshawk and sparrowhawk, flown from the fist straight at the quarry. Stays in Portuguese with its gloss (D4). 'caça em baixo-voo' → 'hunting in baixo-voo'.
Falconry with long-winged falcons that climb and stoop on the quarry from above. Stays in Portuguese with its gloss (D4).
In falconry, taming a new bird to people and handling.
